All drawn from `results/tables/` as delivered by experiment-repo, nothing synthetic.
  > 
  > **Use.** Figures: `\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/figN_...}` (made at 5.5 in, no rescaling; heights Fig 1 2.05, Fig 2 4.5, Fig 3 4.3, Fig 4 4.35, Fig 5 2.6, Fig 6 2.5 in; smallest text 7 pt, sub/superscripts 6 pt). Tables: `\input{tables/tabN_...}` inside your `table` environment (needs `booktabs`; each is a `{\footnotesize ...}` group, fits 5.5 in; captions above). Files: `fig1_concept`, `fig2_headline`, `fig3_margin`, `fig4_budget`, `fig5_floors`, `fig6_certificate`; `tab1_design`, `tab2_guidance`, `tab3_certificate`, `tabA1_sensitivity` (appendix A1), `tabA2_h1` (H1 contrasts, appendix). Page budget: if 9 pages need ~1.5 in back, Fig 2 row 3 (P_c distribution) and Fig 1 are the first to cut; tell me and I shorten rather than rescale.
  > 
  > **What to see (one sentence each; the claims and numbers are yours to word).**
  > - Fig 1: one instance fixed by the rule (German RF, median exact margin 0.081, instance 36): all 100 default-budget runs return the exact top-3 set, the run gap stays far from 0. At the median margin there is no instability to show; the figure is the concept (the set changes only when the gap crosses 0), not a failure. Needs a second pre-specified instance (smallest-margin quartile) to show a failure; asked of experiment-repo.
  > - Fig 2: the share of instances with P_c^ε ≥ 0.9 (ε = 0.05) is ~1 at the default budget for every cell, but the strict P_c share is lower (at the reference budget 79–100 %, lowest GMSC RF 79 %); mean Pearson ≈ 1 for all m ≥ 3d, i.e. aggregate agreement is high everywhere while strict decision-level agreement is not. Row 3: the tail of per-instance P_c below 1.
  > - Fig 3: failures sit in the smallest-margin quartile: strict P_c at the reference budget averages 0.92 in Q1 (0.77 GMSC RF … 1.0 LR) against ≥ 0.997 in Q2–Q4; P_c^ε ≈ 1 in all quartiles.
  > - Fig 4: (a) φ-error falls with slope ≈ −1/2 in m (LR omitted: zero variance); (b) at equal evaluations the paired Kernel estimator is *worse* than the unchanged shap Kernel (shares of exact instances lower by about 0.05–0.4), permutation-antithetic is within the grey smallest-resolvable band or worse; (c) m* grows as the margin shrinks, close to the c/g² line (open triangles: not reached in the grid).
  > - Fig 5: run-to-run (a) agreement of the top-3 set is 0.91–1.0 at the default budget, far above the noise from the background (b: 0.27–0.69) and from retraining (c: bootstrap 0.14–0.83, seed 0.5–1.0, hyper-parameters 0.14–0.79).
  > - Fig 6 / Table 3 (R1): the certificate is well calibrated like the run-twice score, but the primary contrast (certificate vs the first of two runs) favours run-twice in Brier on all five datasets (+0.019 … +0.049), while the matched contrast (run-twice delivering the mean of its two runs) favours the certificate (−0.014 … −0.026); the delivered runs differ in accuracy, so both are shown. Table 3: the certificate stops rarely at 0.9 (1 % on Pima … 50 % on German) and spends ~20 % fewer evaluations than a flat run with the same share exact on German/ACS-Employment, none on the d ≤ 10 datasets; run-twice stops often but its share exact is lower and a flat run reaches it with fewer evaluations.
  > - Table 1: the design (d, output space, reference, AUC, n, R, default and sampling budgets in evaluations). Table 2: minimum evaluations per margin quartile for P_c^ε ≥ 0.9 on ≥ 90 % of instances; "≤" = reached at the smallest grid budget, "n.r." = not reached in the grid; only cells with a sampling grid (R > 1) appear. - issue_comment created in `figtab-repo`#3 ("Request: figures/ and tables/ on paper-repo dev") by `figtab-repo`  > Correction to the Fig 4 line above (I checked it against `figures/fig4_budget.csv`): (a) the fitted log-log slope of the φ-error against m is −0.59 … −0.65 (CIs from −0.57 to −0.66, none containing −0.5), so "≈ −1/2" is not what the data say: the error falls *faster* than m^(−1/2) over the grid; the dotted −1/2 line in the panel is the theory reference. (b) The paired Kernel estimator is lower than the unchanged shap Kernel at equal evaluations by 0.19–0.38 in the share of exact instances (P_c) and by 0.04–0.10 in P_c^ε, in all 8 drawn cells, beyond the smallest resolvable difference (0.05–0.07 and 0.01–0.03); permutation-antithetic is indistinguishable from it (differences −0.015 … +0.001, inside the grey band; LR has exactly 0). The other lines stand.
